Answer: B
Reason: The imaging sequence demonstrates initial ground-glass opacities (often mistaken for viral pneumonia like COVID-19) that rapidly progress to dense bilateral consolidations, a pattern characteristic of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage seen in Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis). The subsequent images show complete radiological resolution within a short timeframe (two weeks), which aligns with the clinical course of treated alveolar hemorrhage rather than typical bacterial pneumonia or fibrotic lung diseases.
